_source: Compiled 2026-11-22 for Cambodia model v5 from World Bank WDI API, NIS/ILO labour force tables, and published studies (see per-series sources); WebFetch/WebSearch only.

formal_share.definition: Wage and salaried workers as % of total employment (WDI SL.EMP.WORK.ZS; ILO modelled estimates). Used as a proxy for the formal/wage-sector share; it is NOT the ILO informal-employment rate (CLFS 2019 reports informal employment 88%).
formal_share.note: Fetched 2026-11-22 through WebFetch with the prescribed prompt; 1991-2025 non-null years transcribed (rounded to 4 d.p. for urban and remittances; formal_share to about 12 digits). Modelled series, smooth by construction; the step 2000-2001 (35.2 to 36.8) is in the source.

urban_share.definition: Urban population as % of total (WDI SP.URB.TOTL.IN.ZS, UN WPP-based).
urban_share.note: Fetched 2026-11-22. 1960-2025 non-null years. Series break: 1975-1979 values (4.7-9.2) and 1970-74 (17.6-33.0) reflect the Khmer Rouge evacuation and civil war, not a smooth process; 2018 to 2019 jump (37.6 to 39.6) and the steep 2013-2018 rise are plausibly a reclassification of urban areas (cause not verified here). Model uses 1979 onward.

remittances_gdp.definition: Personal remittances received, % of GDP (WDI BX.TRF.PWKR.DT.GD.ZS; balance-of-payments basis, workers' remittances and compensation of employees).
remittances_gdp.note: Fetched 2026-11-22. Breaks: 1997 to 1998 (0.34 to 2.31) and 2009 to 2010 (1.14 to 4.04) and 2018 to 2019 (4.3 to 7.2) look like compilation/definition breaks rather than real jumps (cause not verified); treat levels across breaks with caution. 1992-2025 non-null years.

bac2_pass_rate.definition: Grade 12 national exam (Bac II) pass rate as used in config.json tertiary_entry_exam.pass_rate: first-sitting rate except 2014 which is the post-resit final rate (40.67; first sitting was 25.72) and 2020 set to 100 (exam cancelled, all passed automatically). Press reports of MoEYS figures.
bac2_pass_rate.note: Carried over from config.json/facts.md; see VERIFICATION in report for items re-checked. 2012-2013 approximate (86-87). 2024 is 79 (106,351 passed). 2025 pass rate 84.5% (122,473 of 144,848 sat) is in bac2_candidates, not added here because only one source (The Star). Pre-2012 default 80 is DECLARED in config, not data.

occ_credential_share.definition: Sum of shares for managers + professionals + technicians and associate professionals + clerical support workers, from NIS CSES labour tables (Table 10, employment population 15-64 by main occupation and sex, CSES 2013 labour force release). Components (mgr/prof/tech/clerk): 2004 1.3/3.8/0.6/0.2; 2007 0.9/3.0/2.0/1.9; 2008 0.8/3.3/2.2/2.5; 2009 0.5/2.5/0.9/1.9; 2010 0.5/2.7/0.9/2.4; 2011 0.6/2.2/0.8/2.3; 2012 0.7/2.5/1.0/2.6; 2013 0.9/2.9/0.9/3.0.
occ_credential_share.note: Read via summarising WebFetch 2026-11-22. CLASSIFICATION BREAK/NOISE: 2004 clerical 0.2% vs 2007 1.9% and 2007-08 technicians 2.0-2.2% vs 0.9% in 2009 point to occupation recoding between CSES rounds (classification version not stated in the table). Not comparable with the 2019 CLFS series (ISCO-08). Years 2005, 2006 not in the table.

occ_credential_share_clfs2019.definition: Managers 1.6 + professionals 4.2 + technicians and associate professionals 3.7 + clerical support workers 1.6 (ISCO-08 major groups, Figure 5.1, Cambodia Labour Force Survey 2019, total employment 7,883,106). Separate series because the CLFS coding (ISCO-08) and population (all employed, 19th ICLS definition) differ from the CSES 2004-2013 series.
occ_credential_share_clfs2019.note: Read via WebFetch 2026-11-22 (Figure 5.1 values; group shares sum to 100.0). Report itself warns some 2019 data are not comparable with the 2012 survey. CEIC (NIS) 2021 headcounts: managers 86k, professionals 267k, technicians 212k, clerical 295k (sum 860k; total employment not given, so no share computed). ILOSTAT API (rplumber.ilo.org) returned binary to the fetch tool and could not be read.

compulsory_years.definition: Years of basic education to which every citizen has a free right in public schools (Law on Education, Royal Kram NS/RKM/1207/032, 8 Dec 2007): Art. 17 basic education = grades 1-9; Art. 31 right to at least 9 years free in public schools; Art. 36 parents must enrol children at age 6 (70 months) in grade 1.
compulsory_years.note: Read via WebFetch 2026-11-22. The text does not use the word 'compulsory' for attendance; the duty is the parental enrolment obligation (Art. 36) and no penalty was seen. UNICEF 2016 (facts.md) says primary education 'is not compulsory'; WDI SE.COM.DURS is null for all years. Treat 9 as 'free basic education with enrolment duty', applied from 2007; no earlier-year value claimed.

premium_tertiary.definition: Wage premium of completed tertiary vs completed secondary education, all workers, extended Mincer regression on CLFS 2019 (WB 2024 Table 3.3). Not annualised. Male 33.2, female 26.0, urban 31.1, rural 23.0.
premium_tertiary.note: World Bank 2024 Table 3.3 reports a 30% level premium; converted exactly as ln(1.30) because engine5 requires log points. Original percent retained in this note. CLFS 2019, extended Mincerian, all workers 15+.

premium_tertiary_vs_none.definition: Tertiary vs none/below primary, all workers (WB 2024 Table 3.3). Male 67.2, female 56.7. Different reference group from premium_tertiary; do not splice.
premium_tertiary_vs_none.note: World Bank 2024 'Reimagining Higher Education in Cambodia', Table 3.3 (authors' calculations from CLFS 2019, extended Mincerian, all workers 15+). Read via WebFetch 2026-11-22 (summarised extract of the PDF). The matching row in demand_costs.md was labelled 'CSES'; the table source is the 2019 Cambodia Labour Force Survey.

premium_tertiary_annualised_wb.definition: Annualised return to tertiary vs secondary. 2019: WB 2024 Table 3.3 (CLFS 2019). 2008: Montenegro and Patrinos (2014) as quoted in WB 2024 Section 3.2.3; method and sample of the 2008 figure not read, so the two points may not be strictly comparable.
premium_tertiary_annualised_wb.source: https://openknowledge.worldbank.org/bitstreams/b9d36ecb-f91b-49b3-ad34-c09e1043e1a7/download ; Montenegro and Patrinos 2014 (quoted, original not read)
premium_tertiary_annualised_wb.note: Both numbers seen in the WB 2024 text/table this session. WB 2024 suggests graduate supply may have outpaced demand but also notes 2019 conditions may have been unusual. The 2008 point is secondary-quoted.

premium_tertiary_annualised_sakellariou_.definition: Annualised return to university vs upper secondary, wage employees 22-65, log hourly wage, SES 2003-04 (Sakellariou 2008, NTU EGC WP 2008-05, Table 6 / text 'highest premiums ... 10% for men and 12% for women'). Men's value stored; women 12.
premium_tertiary_annualised_sakellariou_.note: The 10%/12% figures are from the paper's text as relayed by a summarising fetch; the Table 6 university row read through the same tool shows 0.001 (men) and -0.015 (women), which contradicts the text and the column alignment is unclear. Treat as unreliable until read from the PDF. 2003-04 survey keyed as 2004. 1997 university value not reliably extracted.

premium_secondary.definition: Wage premium of completed secondary vs completed primary education, all workers, extended Mincer on CLFS 2019 (WB 2024 Table 3.3). Male 19.8, female 19.2, urban 20.7, rural 16.9. Annualised 3.5%/yr.
premium_secondary.note: World Bank 2024 Table 3.3 reports a 21% level premium; converted exactly as ln(1.21) because engine5 requires log points. Original percent retained in this note. CLFS 2019, extended Mincerian, all workers 15+.

premium_secondary_vs_none.definition: Secondary vs none/below primary, all workers (WB 2024 Table 3.3). Primary vs none 17.0; annualised primary 5.7. Different reference group from premium_secondary; do not splice.
premium_secondary_vs_none.note: World Bank 2024 'Reimagining Higher Education in Cambodia', Table 3.3 (authors' calculations from CLFS 2019, extended Mincerian, all workers 15+). Read via WebFetch 2026-11-22 (summarised extract of the PDF). The matching row in demand_costs.md was labelled 'CSES'; the table source is the 2019 Cambodia Labour Force Survey.

premium_ols_loghourly_wb2019.unit: log points, tertiary vs no formal education (OLS, monthly wage per WB Table 3.4)
premium_ols_loghourly_wb2019.definition: WB 2024 Table 3.4 OLS coefficient for tertiary education, reference no formal education, n=9,377, controls: experience, sex, sector, rural, industry, high-skill occupation, province. Secondary 0.1596, primary 0.0421. Quantile range for tertiary 0.28 (median) to 0.44 (q90).
premium_ols_loghourly_wb2019.note: Table 3.4 controls include a high-skill occupation dummy and sector, so it nets out part of the credential premium (compare Table 3.3). Stored only tertiary; secondary 0.1596.

mincer_return_per_year_sakellariou_men.unit: % per year of schooling (log hourly wage x100)
mincer_return_per_year_sakellariou_men.definition: OLS Mincer return per year of schooling, men, wage employees 22-65 (Sakellariou 2008 Table 4); SES 1997 and SES 2003-04 (keyed 2004). Women: 1997 1.5 (t=1.2, insignificant), 2003-04 6.2. IV men 2003-04 9.6.
mincer_return_per_year_sakellariou_men.note: Table 4/10 values read via WebFetch 2026-11-22; N men 1,261 (1997) and 1,825 (2003-04). Per-year return, not a level premium; do not splice with premium_secondary/tertiary.

premium_secondary_annualised_sakellariou.unit: % per year (annualised), men, upper secondary vs lower secondary
premium_secondary_annualised_sakellariou.definition: Sakellariou 2008 Table 6 annualised return to upper secondary vs lower secondary, men, log hourly wage, wage employees 22-65. Women 1997 12.1, 2003-04 7.4. Lower secondary vs primary men 3.8 (1997) / 1.2 (2003-04).
premium_secondary_annualised_sakellariou.note: Table 6 as read through a summarising fetch tool; the tool warned the university row contradicts the text and the column alignment is unclear, so the whole table is flagged. Use only as order-of-magnitude.
